references.text: The same warning of defeat for enemies as punishment for disobedience to God, where Israel will flee even though no one pursues them.
Describes fleeing in fear of enemies and lack of resistance, a parallel theme of God's judgment through military defeat.
The opposite blessing where enemies will flee by seven roads, contrasting with the curse in verse 25.
Israel's defeat at Ai illustrates the fulfillment of this curse when the people sinned.
Israel's defeat against the Philistines and the loss of the ark of the covenant show the consequence of disobedience to God.
The prophecy that a thousand will flee from one threat, reflecting the curse of fleeing before enemies.
Judah shall become a terror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a direct linguistic parallel to becoming 'a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth'.
Jeremiah's prophecy that Israel will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, fulfilling Moses' warning.
The same expression about becoming a curse and a horror among all peoples, reflecting the curse in Deuteronomy.
God will make them a terror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a direct fulfillment of the curse.
